lines.text: Louisville, 1954. Someone steals a twelve-year-old's bike, and he tells a cop he's going to whup the thief.
The cop runs a boxing gym. Learn to fight first, he says.
Six years later, Cassius Clay is an Olympic champion. At twenty-two, he takes the heavyweight title from the most feared man in boxing.
Then he changes his name to Muhammad Ali. And when the Army drafts him in 1967, he refuses to step forward.
They strip his title, take his license, and sentence him to five years. The man who'd fight anyone loses three and a half years of his prime over the one fight he refused.
He comes back slower, and Joe Frazier hands him his first loss. Months later, the Supreme Court clears him, eight to nothing.
Zaire, 1974. He leans on the ropes, lets George Foreman punch himself out, and knocks him down in the eighth. Champion again.
Twenty-two years later, his hands shake from Parkinson's as he lights the Olympic flame.
He never found the kid who stole his bike.
